preRegisteredFalsifier.whatWouldProveReading2WrongAndMechanismA: An authority that is neither this program nor Hays CAD -- specifically the Texas Comptroller PTAD (Property Value Study certified totals, or a Methods and Assistance Program review) -- publishing a Hays County (CAD 105 / county 48209) account or parcel count for tax year 2025 or 2026 that lands materially above 134,606, in the neighborhood of 172,000 or higher. A number that size from an authority with statutory oversight of every Texas CAD's roll, computed from Hays CAD's own certified submissions to the state, cannot be explained by anything in our pipeline -- it would mean Hays CAD itself is reporting a much larger roll to the state than the file it publishes for public bulk download contains, which reopens mechanism A (or a new mechanism C: a bulk-download-vs-certified-roll gap) as a real, load-bearing problem for launch.
preRegisteredFalsifier.expectedNumberIfReading2Holds: At or near 134,600 (allow normal roll growth/PVS-methodology variance, call it +/- 10 percent, so a PTAD figure anywhere in roughly 121,000-148,000 counts as confirming). This is the number this lane expects going in, based on three prior independent re-derivations, but none of those three shared an authority outside this program and Hays CAD, which is exactly the gap this lane exists to close.

decisionRule.nearOrBelow134600: Reading 2 confirmed by an external authority. Report plainly: Hays CAD is not missing 30,000+ properties; the state's own oversight body agrees the roll is this size.
decisionRule.near172000OrHigher: Falsifier FIRES. Mechanism A is reopened. Report loudly: this is a real acquisition gap on a launch county, not a baseline-inflation artifact, and needs an operator-level response before Hays launches.
decisionRule.somethingElseEntirelyDifferent: e.g. PTAD reports a number keyed to a different unit (parcels vs. accounts vs. taxable-value-weighted count) or does not break out Hays separately -- report the number, what it counts, and state explicitly that it neither confirms nor refutes reading 2, rather than forcing it into one bucket.
